q1_issues.issue: "reached the Hollows" has a bare direct object, which the instruction set's own worked example encodes as (Theme sk_reach_1 sk_platform_1); Goal is the head for a spatial "to"-oblique and mis-slots the object here.

Definite/indefinite plural subjects with distributive predicates get no per-member distribution rule (burned 14-17, showed 23-27, survived 62-65, fled 67-70, reached 71-74, left 83-87) even though the same rule form is emitted for the sky-cat group at 49, 56 and 79.
"The mist-light" is a definite, specific referent but is filled by the bare kind symbol mist_light, which also occupies a class slot at statement 18, so one symbol serves as both kind and individual.
"left silken threads on the lanterns" makes the threads Patient, but they are deposited unchanged, and the "does the object change?" test plus the default-to-Theme rule point to Theme.

q2_gaps: An ordinal day-of-year date in a non-Gregorian calendar ("On day 300 of Year 1") — the Time section defines (Day n) as a day-of-month term composing with Month/Year, and gives no form for a day number counted within a year.

A mass noun re-mentioned as a definite referent and filling a subject role ("produced mist-light" ... "The mist-light attracted nightmoths") — the Existential section says a definite mints a typed sk_ witness while a non-specific mass object stays a bare kind constant, and nothing decides which applies.
notes: Name handling (Harbor Row, the plural-label Hollows), group/cardinality shape, compound decomposition, day-part times and the collective reading of "together" all follow the instruction set closely. The pre-nominal participle in "the surviving nightmoths" is recorded nowhere, though Core patterns bars silently dropping a stated modifier.
